sections.text: Aquatic ecosystems cover ~71% of Earth's surface (ocean) and host the majority of Earth's biodiversity at the phylum level. They share core ecological principles with terrestrial systems but differ fundamentally in: three-dimensional structure (water column), the dominance of dissolved nutrients and gases, the short lifespan of primary producers (phytoplankton turnover in days vs trees in centuries), and the role of stratification in controlling productivity and oxygen.

sections.text:
```
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|              AQUATIC ECOSYSTEM TYPES                          |
|                                                               |
|  FRESHWATER                 MARINE                            |
|  ┌──────────┐               ┌──────────────────────────────┐  |
|  │  Lakes   │               │ Open ocean (pelagic)         │  |
|  │  Ponds   │               │ Coastal shelf                │  |
|  │  Streams │               │ Estuaries (transition zone)  │  |
|  │  Rivers  │               │ Coral reefs                  │  |
|  │  Wetlands│               │ Kelp forests                 │  |
|  │  Bogs    │               │ Deep sea / hydrothermal vents│  |
|  └──────────┘               └──────────────────────────────┘  |
|                                                                |
|  TRANSITIONAL: Estuaries (freshwater + saltwater mixing)      |
|                Mangroves, salt marshes                        |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```
